mission.title: Pernicious Hour
mission.description: Help move the General's soldiers out of the Machines' reach, see that the Trainman and the Effectuator handle the transfer, and report to the Merovingian.

npc.say: You ask too many questions. What's your game?
Psst! I'm not so sure about this guy! I think he's lost a few sprockets lately, if ya know what I mean!
I don't see how you could put anything past the Machines at this point.
Quite simple, you know: they couldn't face the fact that he's gone, so they've invented him again. Easiest thing in the world, when people really want to believe it.
Yes... He will betray everyone, and everything. I learned that long ago. Now...I depend upon it.
The old man shouldn't have messed with the kid. That was his big mistake right there.
I hear that female Agent we hit has come back with a vengeance. I'd like a crack at her.

phase.briefing:
Oh, it's you, {player}. Didn't go to see the Apothecary off, then? Too bad, too bad... Apparently you missed quite a show.
The General has found himself in something of a pinch; it seems that the Machines are quite systematically shutting down his operation. What to do, eh? Naturally, he wants us to pull his soldiers out of the fire that's licking his polished boots. And we'll be tickled to help.
Why don't you go get the details from him, operative? He seems to like you. As if we needed more proof that he's a few frags short of a set...

enter.say:
Huh... I heard the Merv basically sold the Apothecary up the river to the Machines, and got her deleted. You don't think Flood had maybe just a little crush on her, do you? No, really! Remember how he wouldn't shut up about how she was an artist and stuff?
Okay, you should be finding the General, or his hologram or whatever, in there. I've got some of his soldier-boys on my scope.

done.say: Sounds like he's even a little shy about hanging around in hologram form now. Those Machines must really be up his tailpipe.

talk.say: Ah, good. I have several more troop transfers I need, both from within the city, and from Stalingrad. These are time-sensitive. I'll have my men send the details to your operator.

done.say: Shee--! He's pretty sure we're gonna jump right to it like good little soldiers, isn't he?

near.say: Hm... No sign of the brass yet. Have a word with the tank jockey in there.

phase.briefing:
Two transfers, eh? This looks to be a more profitable day than I'd supposed.
Confirm that the soldiers in the city are ready for transport.

enter.say:
I'm telling you, he's crying over her--on the inside.
Mm-kay... Got a trooper showing in there. Hm, guess the others are Elites. I'm sure they'll just be pleased as punch to see you.

done.say:
Whoops! Machines are rushing the place!
Uh... I don't suppose you could rally up any of the commandos to help out?
Man, the Machines are on the General like kids on cake! The guy's starting to become a downright liability.

phase.briefing:
The Trainman and the Effectuator will be handling the transportation chores, operative, although if you ask me, you'd be hard-pressed to find two less-dependable programs in the Merovingian's employ. Only fitting, I suppose, since you're the one working with them. How I'm meant to get anything accomplished with the dull tools they give me, I simply don't know...
Try to see to it that they're on-task, would you? The Machines are leaving us no room for error.

enter.say:
Looks like they're both in there. No hostiles on-scope...
Hold on a sec... I thought the Trainman handled transportation between the Matrix and the Machine mainframes. What's he got to do with moving the General's programs?

talk.say: You again? Tell that lap-dog to mind his own business. My shipment will leave on time.

done.say: So he is moving commandos. But the General wouldn't want them going to the Machines! Something's up...
Even the Machines don't know parts of their servers like I do. They won't find them.

talk.say:
Hah! Tell Floodsy-wudsy to keep his muffs on. We'll have those straight-shooters safely stowed where the Machines can't get 'em!
'Course, we'll tell the General that the Machines did get 'em. Heh. Wink, wink!

phase.briefing: I know you assume otherwise, operative, but believe it or not, I haven't got all day free to explain everything to you in small words. Go report the transport status to the Merovingian, and stop bothering me.

enter.say:
Yep, he totally holds the Apothecary thing against us.
Okay, so we know that we're shipping commandos out of the main simulation, without telling the General about it.
Hm... Sounds to me like the General just ran out of friends.

talk.say:
My wife is a demanding woman... Eh, Persephone?
You would think she would be satisfied with my disposing of the Apothecary for her...but c'est la guerre.
Ah, and Le General will learn something about war as well, non? But not quite yet. His ignorance will still have its use...for a time.

done.say:
Man! The Merv has been playing the General this whole while?
Hah. I knew we were working for the right guy.

Trust no one, {player}, especially not those you most wish to trust. No matter how much they may deny it--may not even realize it--even the most charitable person always works precisely in their own interest.
N'oubliez jamais ceci.

near.say: It's the Machines, obviously--another trick to keep the humans in line, like with the Cryptos fellow.
No, no, no... They haven't got the stones. It's those cultish ones, I tell you.
Quite simple, you know: they couldn't face the fact that he's gone, so they've invented him again. Easiest thing in the world, when people really want to believe it.
I don't see how you could put anything past the Machines at this point.
Yes... He will betray everyone, and everything. I learned that long ago. Now...I depend upon it.

mission.finish:
It's a dog-eat-dog world, operative, which is why I prefer to dine alone. The General's soldiers are fated to fatten the pack, and the Apothecary... Hm... She, after all, was merely served her own supper.
Always watch your own back, {player}, because goodness knows, nobody else wants to look at it.
The Apothecary's legacy, however, lives on in the deadly code she compiled. Our people have put the final touches on her kill-code for the Oracle. Now, how to catch a fortune-teller by surprise?
